title: diagram
description: A diagram, drawn as inline SVG and checked for overlaps and overflowing text (frames may cross, and a frame's label is held to the frame's width, not its height or a canvas written): its title, what it shows for a reader who cannot see it, and a canvas of width by height (either left out, as far as what is drawn reaches and 20 more) with the parts placed on it, a graph of boxes and edges that floe lays out among them; or example, the name of a built-in one, which floe diagram example lists; floe diagram guide says how to write a diagram

example.description: A kind of diagram floe diagram example lists, drawn in the page's language

width.description: Left out, as far right as what is drawn reaches and 20 more; raw SVG is not measured, so write it with raw

height.description: Left out, as far down as what is drawn reaches and 20 more; raw SVG is not measured, so write it with raw

title.description: What the diagram shows, for a reader who cannot see it

items.description: One key naming the kind of the part

canvas.description: Up to ten million, past where coordinates and sizes written reach (two million), so that a canvas floe tells can be written

coord.description: A coordinate, within a million either way, so that what floe works out from it stays finite and of a sane size

text.description: Text, or its words in each language by tag, English among them: {en: …, ja: …}

name.description: The name an edge's from or to, or a graph's with, gives, unique in the diagram

viaPoint.description: A point to turn at, [x, y], or one axis, { x } or { y }: the other is the point before's, the first point's the centre of the edge's start

origin.description: What x is: the left edge (the default) or the centre

end.description: The name of a part, a named row or a node, or a point [x, y]

frame.description: A box around other parts, its label inside the top left corner, or right of its icon. Frames are not checked against one another, so they may cross, and a frame's label is held to the frame's width, not its height or a canvas written

icon.description: An icon in the corner, its label to the right of it

box.description: A box of centred rows of text, as wide and tall as they need when w and h are left out

rows.description: Each a text, or [text, style]; without a style the first is main and the rest sub

table.description: A heading over rows of a name and a type (an ER entity, a class)

rows.description: Each [name, type] or [name], --- for a separator, or {name, cells: [name, type]} for a row an edge can end at

icon.description: An icon of an icon set (aws/…, gcp/…, azure/…, found with floe icons search) with its top left at x, y; with a label, its bottom side, where an edge ends, is under the label

edge.description: A line from one end to another: right-angled through via, or straight from point to point with straight

dot.description: A circle (a commit, a milestone, a start state); an edge naming it ends at its outline

bar.description: A horizontal span (a timeline period), its label to the right

axis.description: A time axis with labelled ticks, and grid lines up to grid; a tick's text is drawn at it, or between it and the next tick (labels: between); a tick of empty text is a mark alone

labels.description: Where a tick's text goes: at the tick (the default), or halfway between it and the next tick on its right, or x2 past the last

circle.description: A translucent circle that may overlap others (a Venn diagram)

label.description: Text at x, y, or in the area of a Venn diagram inside the circles of in and outside the others

anchor.description: Only where x and y place the label; with in alone, leave it out

plain.description: No background, for text on a coloured area: the default for a label with in, which stands on a circle; false gives one a background

line.description: A line without arrows: a line, a lifeline or a divider

tree.description: A tree of boxes, its root's centre at x and top at y: floe places each node under its parent and draws the edges

graph.description: Boxes and the edges between them, which floe lays out in ranks, the top left of all of it at x and y; the edges of one graph may cross one another
graph.$comment: LIMIT: neither nodes nor lanes is told only as missing nodes, both (or lanes: true with nodes) only as an additional property nodes, naming no lanes: the library tells one rule's words, and oneOf or anyOf tell none of theirs

then.$comment: LIMIT: the keys every graph takes but nodes, copied: add a key to properties here too, or a graph of lanes refuses it as an additional property. A mistake is told at the graph, not at its nodes, and a misspelt key beside nodes is told twice, here and by the graph's own additionalProperties

direction.description: Which way the edges run: down (the default) or right

lanes.description: In place of nodes: lanes, each a group, a band from end to end of the graph along its edges, in the order written; a graph holds 200 boxes, icons, groups and lanes at most, all counted together through its groups and lanes

graphNodes.description: Boxes, icons and groups of them; a graph holds 200 boxes, icons, groups and lanes at most, all counted together through its groups and lanes

items.description: One key naming the kind of the node

graphGroup.description: Boxes and groups kept side by side in every rank, framed, its label in the frame's top left corner; an edge of the graph may end at it by its name, at the frame's top or bottom, unless it is a lane

icon.description: An icon in the frame's corner, its label to the right of it

graphIcon.description: An icon of the graph, 48 square with its label below, with no box round it; the n edges at a side end at the points that part it into n+1 equal parts, the icon's own side, or under its label

icon.description: The icon's name, as for the part icon

graphWith.description: The box or icon of the graph this one stands in one rank with, an edge drawn or not. An edge from a box into this one then does not decide ranks, and runs up or down as the ranks fall

graphBox.description: A box of the graph, as wide and tall as its rows need, or wider for the edges at a side

graphEdge.description: An edge between boxes or groups of the graph, by name; from and to the same box, a loop out of the side the graph's edges between ranks do not use (an edge written level may not take that side); at a group, it ends at the frame's top or bottom

label.description: Words on the edge, cutting it; the drawing grows where they lack room, the ranks and the order as with no label

level.description: Whether its two boxes stand in one rank, the edge straight between their facing sides (or bent, at an icon with more than one edge on a side, whose point stands off its line): two boxes of one group, standing as written, or directly in two lanes, at their lanes' ends towards each other; on a loop it changes nothing

graphMarker.description: An arrowhead or none: the others are wider than the room the edges of a graph keep between them

raw.description: SVG no part draws, of SVG's elements alone, without script or foreignObject (which a page takes elsewhere) or an element a page refuses, left out of the checks. Colour it with the variables of the palette's table in the docs (fill="var(--accent)"), and in a tone by data-floe-tone on it or on a <g> around it within the raw SVG and var(--tone). Give text fill="currentColor" (--fg) and font-size="12": without them it draws black at the page's size. A part's classes, data-floe-look and data-floe-part are floe's own
